memory_update.text: LOPE is the strongest direct underfollowed public-market candidate for the online higher-ed fixed-cost stack because its disclosed service bundle maps to marketing, lead acquisition, admissions, financial aid, advising, LMS, CRM, student records, course development, faculty support, scheduling, and hybrid healthcare lab infrastructure.

STRA should be tracked not only as an online higher-ed operator but as an employer-channel and education-benefits infrastructure asset through ETS, Sophia Learning, Workforce Edge, and employer-affiliated enrollment.

COUR remains relevant to the node as a small-cap platform layer for degrees, campus, enterprise, government, credit-bearing certificates, and workforce credentials, but evidence must verify institutional durability and degree economics.

Need a later pass on private or recently delisted OPM/student-information-system vendors such as 2U, Instructure, PowerSchool, Anthology, Ellucian, and niche enrollment-marketing firms because many direct chokepoint assets may not currently be US-listed.

The core bottleneck is not content alone; it is the capitalized and operationally complex stack of student acquisition, compliance-aware admissions, financial aid, advising, retention analytics, SIS/LMS/CRM integration, course development, and employer/workforce distribution.

node: Online higher-education enrollment, marketing, student services, and retention infrastructure
summary: Expanded the underfollowed universe around the fixed-cost online higher-education stack: student acquisition, admissions, advising, employer channels, degree platforms, retention infrastructure, and workforce-aligned online programs. The strongest direct node match is Grand Canyon Education because its disclosed services map almost exactly to the outsourced online-program fixed-cost stack. Strategic Education and Coursera are included as underfollowed software/platform or employer-channel assets rather than simple education operators. Stride is included as an adjacent reference/underfollowed hybrid because most revenue is K-12, but its Career Learning and adult/talent-development businesses create second-order exposure to online workforce training infrastructure.
